body.statement: On \(\mathcal M^{\beta}_{K,\varepsilon}(B_{\mathrm H})\) with \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\), can the handle \(\mathfrak F\) produce a label-stable coherent estimator using tensor-product B-splines of total dimension \(s_n\asymp n^{(d_X+1)/(2\beta+d_X+1)}\), with the common permutation chosen from the \(K!\) possibilities to maximize the empirical training-sample minimum diagonal-minus-largest-off-diagonal self-report probability, such that every coordinate \(r_m,r_\pi,r_A,r_Z,r_f,r_w,r_W,r_B,r_d,r_D,r_R,r_N,r_h,r_G,r_b\) is \(O_P(\rho_n)\) for \(\rho_n=n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d_X+1)}\)? These coordinatewise rates imply \(R_{\Sigma}=O_P(\rho_n)=o_P(1)\) and \(\Delta_n=O_P(\rho_n^2)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\), while \(w\), \(W\), \(B\), \(d\), \(D\), \(R\), \(N\), \(h\), \(G\), \(b_{(\cdot)}\), and \(b_U\) remain plug-in implications rather than separately fitted nuisances.
body.justification: The named H\"older class, spline schedule, modal-gap label rule, and coordinatewise target rates make the implementation question falsifiable while leaving efficient inference conditional on their attainment.
body.gap: Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin estimate repeated-measurement mixtures, while Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen use an iterative sieve method; neither analyzes the new projected score with all derived nuisances constrained to one fitted law.
body.consumer: A construction would provide the implementable first stage for the augmented maternal-smoking analysis and prevent first-order bias from incoherent nuisance fits.

obligation.what_is_open: A proof that the specifically prescribed global tensor-product B-spline product-likelihood fit and empirical-minimum label rule attain the four primitive factor rates uniformly enough to stay in the fixed-rank half-margin set.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen assumptions specify Hölder membership but do not specify the spline boundary/extension convention on the general outcome support, the constrained likelihood parameterization, a local likelihood-curvature inequality, or the uniform-norm control needed by the minimum-over-training-points label selector.  Those facts do not follow from the finite projector algebra.
obligation.attempted: Reduced all derived nuisance rates to the four primitive rates by inverse identities and fixed-rank pseudoinverse perturbation; checked that \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\) makes the resulting squared rate negligible at root \(n\).  A direct sieve-likelihood proof stops at the missing curvature and uniform label-selection premises.
obligation.partial_result: The regular-stratum algebra does prove the following propagation statement: if one constrained, label-aligned primitive fit satisfies \(r_\pi+r_A+r_Z+r_f=O_P(\rho_n)\), then bounded integration gives \(r_m=O_P(\rho_n)\), and the inverse, Bayes, projector, and fixed-rank pseudoinverse identities give every derived coordinate \(r_w,r_W,r_B,r_d,r_D,r_R,r_N,r_h,r_G,r_b=O_P(\rho_n)\).  Consequently \(R_\Sigma=O_P(\rho_n)\) and \(\Delta_n=O_P(\rho_n^2)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\) when \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\).  What is not proved from the frozen primitives is that the specifically named product-likelihood B-spline fit, with the empirical-minimum permutation rule, attains the four primitive rates without additional likelihood curvature, spline-domain, and uniform label-selection conditions.
